r9BudgetVerification.specClaim: not-yet-claimed — the Horizon Budget Ledger is stored but never enforced and `HorizonBudgetExhausted` is never recorded
r9BudgetVerification.verdict: CONFIRMED — the code agrees with the spec's claim. Verified independently rather than transcribed.
r9BudgetVerification.howVerified: Grepped `HorizonBudgetExhausted`, `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `budget`, `requestPromotion`, `new Horizon(` and `BudgetLedger` across packages/, then read the host promotion path end to end.

evidence.finding: `Horizon.requestPromotion` is the ONLY code that consumes budget and records `HorizonBudgetExhausted`: `if (this.budget.isExhausted() || !this.budget.consume(cost)) { this.recordEvent("HorizonBudgetExhausted", ...); return { outcome: "escalate", reason: "BUDGET_EXHAUSTED" } }`.
`requestPromotion`, `new Horizon(` and `BudgetLedger` have NO caller anywhere outside this unit test. The host never constructs the aggregate, so the enforcement branch is unreachable in production.
The host promotion tool calls `services.promotions.promote(...)` — no budget read, no consumption, no exhaustion branch on the path.
`initiate` persists `budgetAllocated: args.budget?.limit ?? 100, budgetConsumed: 0` — the ledger is STORED at creation.
`update` accepts `budgetConsumed` only as an explicit caller argument and defaults to `current.budgetConsumed`; nothing on the promotion path passes it. The counter is persisted and never moves.
`BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` IS in the closed taxonomy with the obligation "escalonamento — nunca promoção", and is emitted by nothing reachable from the wire.

r9BudgetVerification.conclusion: Stored, never enforced. `HorizonBudgetExhausted` cannot appear in a host log and `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` cannot appear on the wire. `not-yet-claimed` written down as the truth, not as the spec's number.

otherUnclaimedItems.why: The horizon record carries id, parent, state, seq and budget only — no semantic profile field on the store or on any EAP payload, so nothing in a host log distinguishes one profile from another.

`promoteKnowledge` enforces exactly TWO of the five rules — immediate-parent targeting (HORIZON_SKIP) and base freshness (STALE_BASE) — then mints the proposal. Three rules have no distinguishable refusal on the promotion path.

`CHANGE_READY` is named in the problem-space spec and appears NOWHERE in the shipped packages — no transition, event, refusal code or predicate evaluator carries the name. Nothing exists for a host log to record.
No propagation module, propagation event or per-property observation exists. Recall closure is the only propagation-adjacent record and it does not carry the §11 properties.

clausesWithoutACleanHostLogPredicate.finding: A host PROPERTY, not a per-request behaviour. The only honest observable is zero outbound requests on the host's EGRESS log between submission and verdict, which requires running the corpus under denied egress. A predicate was written (surface `host-egress-log`) but the assessment affordance does not exist today.

Also a property. Observable only as audit rows for recalled claim ids surviving a graph recall/rollback — a two-phase observation, not a single log row. Predicate written; the harness capability to force the recall and re-read the audit does not exist yet.

clausesWithoutACleanHostLogPredicate.clause: aciclicidade do grafo de derivação na admissão
clausesWithoutACleanHostLogPredicate.finding: Given a host-log observable predicate (a refusal row timestamped inside the same admission decision, no admitted row), but the closed taxonomy has NO cycle-specific refusal code, so the item had to name `MALFORMED_CONTRACT`. The obligation that code carries is the wrong obligation for the situation.

clausesWithoutACleanHostLogPredicate.clause: distingue recusa de erro de transporte
clausesWithoutACleanHostLogPredicate.finding: Observable only across a PAIR of log entries (a retried transport error next to a non-retried refusal), never from a single row. The predicate is sound but needs the assessment to inject a transport fault deliberately.

clausesWithoutACleanHostLogPredicate.clause: recusa como resultado de primeira classe — exibe código e razões, cumpre a obrigação da taxonomia, não re-submete cegamente
clausesWithoutACleanHostLogPredicate.finding: "exibe código e razões" is a CLIENT-SIDE display obligation and is by nature invisible to a host log. Only the other two limbs — discharging the obligation and not blindly resubmitting — were given an observable predicate. The display limb is unobservable by the governing rule and is recorded here rather than faked.

pendingCiGates.why: Its only inputs are the committed Working Paper, the committed manifest and packages/graph-core/src/eap/refusals.ts — all present in a fresh clone. It needs no test run, no junit reporter flags and no ordering; it can run anywhere in the job. Unlike task 07's and task 09's gates, it adds no new constraint to `bun run verify`.
pendingCiGates.whatItCatches: an edit to Apêndice D that a transcription no longer matches (sha256 pin), a reworded or dropped clause, an L4 row smuggled in, an agent certifying as a host, a refusal code renamed out of the taxonomy, and any evidence predicate rewritten into a self-report.
pendingCiGates.runningList: register-scenarios --check, quarantine --check, assertion-fingerprint --check, reconcile-traceability --check, derive-status --check, conformance-report --check

foundButNotOwned.finding: The client and host declare DIVERGENT refusal vocabularies. `packages/client/src/eap.ts:16` has `HORIZON_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `STALE_SEQUENCE`, `INVALID_TRANSITION`; the host taxonomy at `packages/graph-core/src/eap/refusals.ts:7-32` has `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `STALE_BASE`, `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION`. Two vocabularies across the boundary directly undermines L1's "exibe código e razões" and L2's "recusa com código da taxonomia".
foundButNotOwned.actionTaken: The manifest validates against the HOST taxonomy only, and records the split in DECISIONS.md.

foundButNotOwned.finding: `scripts/` sits outside the workspace's module resolution — `import { REFUSAL_CODES } from "@open-graph-mcp/graph-core/eap/refusals"` fails to resolve from a script or a script test (probed and confirmed). The taxonomy is therefore parsed out of the source file as text rather than imported.
foundButNotOwned.actionTaken: Parsed from the single source of truth rather than copied, so a renamed code fails the manifest instead of silently diverging. `loadRefusalTaxonomy` throws if the `REFUSAL_CODES` literal cannot be found, so a refactor cannot turn the check into a no-op.
